checkedAlternates.risk: A rainbow is made of sunlight, so a player may read it as belonging with the sun rather than with the cloud.
checkedAlternates.resolution: A rainbow needs raindrops to bend the light; without water in the air there is no rainbow, which is what the cloud pairing shows.

checkedAlternates.risk: The sun and the rainbow appear together in the same sky and are linked in every childhood drawing.
checkedAlternates.resolution: The sun is the only object on the board that is not on Earth at all, which is why it is the single-item row.

checkedAlternates.risk: A hot-air balloon drifts with the wind and floats the way a cloud does.
checkedAlternates.resolution: A balloon is built and flown by people, alongside the aeroplane and the helicopter.

checkedAlternates.risk: A dragonfly is nicknamed a helicopter in several languages, and it hovers the same way.
checkedAlternates.resolution: A dragonfly is alive, which is the whole of the fourth row.

authorReview.notes: The rows walk outward and then back: one object beyond the Earth, two made of its water, three built by people, four alive.

blindPlaytest.notes: Watch the bat. If testers reject it because they expect a bird row, the fix is the row label, not the item: "Living things that fly" already avoids saying birds.
